references.text: The preceding verse dealing with baldness on the back of the head, which together with verse 41 establishes that baldness in itself does not make a person unclean.
The continuation describing what happens if white or reddish sores appear on the bald area, which may indicate leprosy.
Concerns the priests' prohibition against shaving the head completely bare, showing that baldness had religious significance in Israel.
Isaiah mentions baldness as part of God's judgment, where a shaved head replaces well-groomed hair.
Micah urges cutting off the hair as a sign of mourning, demonstrating the symbolic meaning of baldness.
